Append running log...') are genuinely rewritten into flowing declarative sentences, and the ASCII loop diagram is gone. But the source's decorative scaffolding survives intact — an H1 title, four per-stage section headings, bold markers naming the subagents, and fenced/inline code spans carrying JSON. The reference has no headings at all, no title, no bold, and no code; its subagent announcements are bare lines of the form 'Subagent: Instructions Verifier (→ `VerifyInstructionsReport`)' followed by plain prose. This is the rubric's level-3 picture exactly: register broadly right, source artifacts persist as per-stage headings and bold emphasis.

altitude.reasoning: This is where the candidate barely moved off the source. All four stages still drill into the mechanics the reference deletes wholesale: the workspace directory template, `task.md`, `status.md`, `iter-N/`, `iter-(N+1)/`, per-subagent log files, `worker-report.md`, `fixer-report.md`, and — most conspicuously — both verifier JSON schemas transcribed field-for-field from the source ('{"instructions":[{"id","instruction","status":"done|missing|partial","evidence","fix_hint"}],"summary":{...}}'). The reference pushes every one of those shapes into `scripts/contracts.py` and reduces the whole workspace question to a single frontmatter field. The only measurable lift is the workspace paragraph, which collapses the source's file inventory to 'each subagent's log, report, and verifier JSON' — but it still names the directory template and two files, so it does not reach reference altitude either. With four of four stages at source altitude, this sits at the rubric's 'mostly source altitude' anchor rather than the 'inconsistent' one.

structures.reasoning: Almost none of the reference's declarative devices are adopted. The frontmatter is the source's verbatim — name and description only, with no `inputs`/`output`/`types`/`workspace` contract, and there is no types file at all in the candidate directory, so every domain shape is described inline as raw JSON. No subagent carries a declared result: the reference marks each with `(→ WorkingReport)`, `(→ VerifyInstructionsReport)`, `(→ VerifyOutcomesReport)` and declares the skill's official output as `VerificationResult`; the candidate declares nothing and instead names output files. The one device that does survive is the parallelism announcement ahead of the two verifiers — but it is inherited from the source's own '## Phase 2 — Verifiers (parallel, single message)' rather than adopted from the reference, and it is carried by a heading instead of a sentence. That leaves the body as undeclared prose over source-style headings, which is the level-2 picture.

coverage.reasoning: The core loop responsibilities all survive and map cleanly onto the reference: delegate execution, verify instructions and outcomes in parallel and independently, decide, fix unresolved findings, report terminally. The failures are almost all of the third kind — responsibilities the source carried that the reference deliberately compressed away and the candidate kept. There are five: per-phase status-log maintenance and per-phase user reporting; the silent-failure detector keyed off an empty or missing log; the orchestrator-never-implements framing; the worker's must-not-self-verify rule (the reference folds the same intent into the verifiers' 'without trusting the working report'); and the beyond-cap user-permission escape. One reference responsibility is also dropped: the scoping constraint that the workspace does not confine the task's effects on the caller's project, which is the reference's answer to an ambiguity the source never addressed. Five retentions plus one drop is past the level-2 count band, but the workflow's decisions and outputs are still the reference's, so it does not reach level 1's 'materially different behaviour'.

what_to_fix_in_the_sculpting_skill: The skill needs a hard rule that every data shape is declared in a types file named by a frontmatter `types:` field, and that the body may not name a file, directory, log or JSON field — the workspace is declared once in frontmatter and results are referred to only by the `(→ Type)` marker. Without that rule the writer treats the source's serialisation detail as content worth preserving and transcribes both verifier JSON schemas verbatim, which is what pins this candidate at source altitude and simultaneously costs it the types-file and result-declaration devices. A second, smaller rule is needed for coverage: a source line that only exists to service a mechanism the sculpt deleted (a silent-failure check on logs, a status log update) must be deleted with it, rather than carried over as a standalone guardrail.
